questions.question: What is the primary non-renewable resource used to produce most traditional plastic food packaging?
options: Crude oil and fossil fuels
Volcanic minerals
Atmospheric nitrogen
Plant-derived cellulose

questions.question: Why is plastic waste in landfills and oceans considered a major environmental threat to organisms?
options: It degrades too quickly, releasing heat into the water.
It persists in the environment for a very long time without degrading and can harm wildlife.
It increases the salinity of ocean waters, killing freshwater fish.
It blocks all sunlight from reaching the deep ocean floor.

questions.question: Which of the following describes a more sustainable alternative to traditional petroleum-based plastics for packaging?
options: Synthetic chlorinated polymers
Heavy metal composite foils
Biodegradable bioplastics made from renewable resources
Single-use fluorocarbon sheets

questions.question: What is one of the main beneficial roles that plastic packaging plays in the food supply chain?
options: It increases the nutritional value of foods over time.
It helps prevent food spoilage and reduces food waste.
It eliminates the need for refrigeration entirely.
It naturally cooks the food while on supermarket shelves.

questions.question: When deciding whether to use plastic packaging for a food product, what trade-off must be carefully evaluated?
options: The cost of supermarket shelf space versus the weight of the labels.
The energy used in cooking the food versus the water used to wash it.
The benefits of preventing food spoilage versus the emissions from production and damage to biodiversity.
The aesthetic appeal of the package versus the expiration date of the product.

questions.question: Which human activity is identified as one of the primary drivers behind global deforestation?
options: Building high-rise residential apartments in deserts
Converting natural forest land into areas for agricultural use
Extracting geothermal energy from deep underground
Setting up offshore wind farms

questions.question: What is a direct ecological consequence of widespread deforestation on forest-dwelling organisms?
options: It leads to habitat loss for many species.
It causes an immediate increase in genetic mutations.
It encourages species to develop underwater adaptations.
It decreases the amount of solar radiation reaching the canopy.

questions.question: Which pair of strategies represents effective ways to mitigate biodiversity loss and combat climate change?
options: Increasing industrial pesticide use and expanding desert regions
Changing human diets and undertaking positive land use changes like reforestation and rewilding
Urbanizing all remaining wetlands and increasing fossil fuel extraction
Introducing invasive species and building concrete flood barriers everywhere

questions.question: How does climate change directly increase the difficulty of global food production?
options: By slowing down the rate of plant respiration in the dark
By making extreme weather events more frequent and disruptive
By reducing the gravity of the Earth, which affects plant roots
By converting all freshwater lakes into saltwater reservoirs

questions.question: How can individual dietary choices help limit the progression of global climate change?
options: By eating only foods that have been highly processed in factories
By choosing diets that reduce greenhouse gas emissions associated with food production
By consuming more imported exotic foods that require air freight
By increasing the intake of foods packaged in heavy-gauge non-recyclable plastics

questions.question: Why does clearing forests disrupt the Earth's carbon cycle?
options: Fewer trees are available to absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere for photosynthesis.
It causes the soil to release large amounts of helium gas.
It prevents plants from absorbing oxygen through their root systems.
It increases the amount of ozone created at ground level.

questions.question: What role does carbon dioxide (CO2) play when its concentration increases in the atmosphere?
options: It acts as a cooling agent that prevents solar radiation from entering the atmosphere.
It acts as a greenhouse gas, enhancing the greenhouse effect and contributing to climate change.
It destroys the ozone layer in the troposphere, causing immediate acid rain.
It reacts with nitrogen to form solid ammonium nitrate in the clouds.

questions.question: How does deforestation affect surface water runoff and what is the consequence of this?
options: It decreases surface runoff, causing severe droughts in all agricultural areas.
It leads to more surface runoff, which increases flooding and threatens our food security.
It turns surface runoff into alkaline streams that dissolve limestone structures.
It stops water from evaporating, leading to a complete halt in the water cycle.

questions.question: Why are many species struggling to survive in their native habitats as a result of climate change?
options: The habitats are becoming entirely devoid of gravity.
Atmospheric nitrogen levels have fallen to near zero.
The environmental conditions are changing, meaning species are less well adapted to live there.
Species are suddenly losing their genetic material due to warmer temperatures.

questions.question: How do some species respond to changing habitat conditions caused by climate change to survive, though this option is not available to all?
options: By undergoing rapid physical mutation within a single generation
By migrating to a new habitat with more suitable conditions
By entering a state of permanent hibernation that lasts for decades
By learning to photosynthesize without sunlight

questions.question: Which of the following is a major consequence of climate change and its associated extreme weather events?
options: An increase in the total number of stable ecosystems globally
A significant loss of biodiversity across different ecosystems
The complete stabilization of seasonal temperatures
An immediate decrease in the rate of natural extinction
